claims.claim: **Most infections are mild or self-limiting**, but their non-specific presentation makes them hard to tell apart from serious infection such as malaria.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **In returning travellers, falciparum malaria is the leading serious infection and the leading cause of death.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Common non-travel diseases are more likely than exotic ones.** A serious cause is more likely in children who travelled to visit friends and relatives. Consider non-infectious causes too (e.g. DVT/PE).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Drug-resistant infection or colonisation may have been acquired**, especially if the child was hospitalised.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Ask whether this could be a disease of public health importance** needing immediate infection control; contact the local health department for advice.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspected measles: negative pressure room with airborne precautions.** Possible novel respiratory illness: appropriate precautions.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Haemorrhagic fevers (Ebola, Marburg, Lassa, Crimean-Congo): strict isolation and strict barrier nursing.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Take a travel history:** location and type (country/region, urban/rural, living conditions, altitude) · timing (dates, seasons, duration) · exposures (animals, insect bites, water and food, activities including sexual contact, drug use, tattoos, sick contacts).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check immunisation history** — routine and travel-specific; typhoid vaccine is only about 70% effective. Ask about prophylaxis adherence, nets and repellent, and any healthcare or medicines abroad.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fever is the only finding in most.** ⚠️ **Altered consciousness, haemorrhage or hypotension suggest cerebral malaria or haemorrhagic fever with shock.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Eschar:** rickettsial infection, borrelia, Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever. **Petechiae:** meningococcal disease, viral haemorrhagic fever, rickettsia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Altered conscious state, lethargy or meningism:** cerebral malaria, meningitis, African trypanosomiasis.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fever persisting over 2 weeks:** malaria, EBV, enteric fever, toxoplasmosis, CMV, acute HIV, TB, brucellosis, Q fever, acute schistosomiasis. **Fever starting over 6 weeks after travel:** TB, amoebic liver abscess, acute hepatitis (B, C or E), *P. vivax* or *P. ovale*.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fever alone** (think malaria, typhoid, dengue, hepatitis A): **FBE with thick and thin film**, BGL, blood culture, LFT if jaundiced, serum to store; discuss specific tests with Infectious Diseases.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also consider:** measles serology ± throat or nose PCR · urine microscopy and culture · **CSF in severely unwell children with meningism, encephalopathy or seizures**, after considering whether neuroimaging is needed first.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fever with diarrhoea** (think malaria, typhoid, dengue, hepatitis, cholera, dysentery, travellers' diarrhoea): the fever-alone tests, with stool MCS and OCP added (the latter particularly if prolonged beyond 10 days).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fever with respiratory symptoms** (think malaria, pneumonia, influenza, TB): as for fever alone, plus CXR and a respiratory virus swab including influenza and COVID; discuss TB investigations with Infectious Diseases.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Undifferentiated fever within two years of return from an endemic region → consider malaria.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Travellers' diarrhoea** = more than 3 diarrhoeal episodes in 24 hours after travel, plus cramping, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting or fever.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most children need no empiric treatment** and can be managed as outpatients with GP follow-up.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A sick child may warrant empiric treatment for sepsis, malaria and/or typhoid** — see the individual guidelines or local antimicrobial guidance, and discuss with Infectious Diseases when needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the local paediatric team** for suspected sepsis, malaria or typhoid, or an unclear diagnosis with clinical concern.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider transfer** for severe malaria, a sick child with persistent fever despite basic empiric therapy, or care beyond the local hospital's comfort level.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Fever in the recently returned traveller' (Last updated April 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Fever_in_the_recently_returned_traveller/, retrieved 2026-09-23
